whyItMatters: Reconnaissance is often more visible in volume than in any one read API. Burst SES identity enumeration can indicate active mapping of email infrastructure before abuse.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may repeatedly query SES identities and verification status to inventory usable domains and email addresses quickly.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is attractive because the reconnaissance is cheap, fast, and can provide a complete picture of the SES footprint before policy changes or sending abuse.
threatContext.whyItMatters: Short-window repetition is often the strongest sign that the activity is exploratory rather than a normal administrative spot check.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, defenders may not recognize an active reconnaissance phase that precedes SES misconfiguration or phishing activity.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for SES
loggingRequirements: SES enumeration events must be ingested with accurate timestamps.
The detection engine must support thresholding or windowed aggregation.
Actor identity should be normalized across IAM users and assumed roles.
limitations: Fixed thresholds may need tuning by environment.
Legitimate automation may burst during synchronization or audits.
Some recon may remain low-and-slow and avoid threshold-based detection.

enrichment.description: Determine whether the actor has previously performed SES enumeration and at what volume.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Makes burst behavior more meaningful in context.

enrichment.description: Understand whether the burst aligns with expected maintenance or sync jobs.
examples: ad hoc burst at unusual hour
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Separates legitimate automation from exploratory recon.

enrichment.description: Track whether the same actor moves into SES write actions or other abuse shortly afterward.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Improves confidence when the burst leads to action.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should detect short-window spikes in SES identity-enumeration activity. It should count `ListIdentities` and `GetIdentityVerificationAttributes` calls per normalized actor and fire when the number of calls exceeds the local threshold inside a five-minute window.
conditions: same normalized actor exceeds threshold in a 5-minute window
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Tune the threshold to local SES usage. 2. Normalize IAM users and assumed roles into a stable actor identity. 3. Escalate further when the burst is performed by an unauthorized actor or followed by SES write activity.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when SES identity-enumeration volume exceeds the configured threshold in a short time window.

simulationCommand: for i in {1..6}; do aws ses get-identity-verification-attributes --identities user@example.com; done

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium with tuned thresholds and actor baselines

deployment.scheduling: Near-real-time or short scheduled windows work well because the burst itself is the signal.
considerations: This is the volume-based SES reconnaissance detector.
Threshold tuning is the main implementation dependency.
